# Code of conduct

This project adopts the **[Contributor Covenant, version 2.1](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html)**.
That document is the standard in full: the expected behaviour, the unacceptable behaviour, and the
enforcement guidelines. Everything below is only what the Covenant leaves to the adopting project —
where it applies, and how to report something.

**Adopted by reference rather than copied in.** The linked version is frozen — version 2.1 has its own
permanent address and cannot change under us — so a copy here would add nothing except a second text
to keep in step with the first. This repository's standing rule is that a fact has one authoritative
definition; a code of conduct is no different. The cost is real and worth naming: you have to follow a
link to read the standard rather than finding it in the repository. Translations are at
<https://www.contributor-covenant.org/translations>, and the Covenant's FAQ at
<https://www.contributor-covenant.org/faq>.

## Where it applies

Everywhere this project is worked or represented: issues, pull requests, commit messages and code
review in this repository.

It is worth being plain about the scale. This is one small business's website, not a community
project. Nearly all of the work here is done by the owner and by AI agents working tickets, and there
is no chat room, no forum and no mailing list. The code of conduct is here because a public repository
should say what it expects — not because a problem is anticipated.

## Reporting

Report to the repository owner, **[@nanatsusaya](https://github.com/nanatsusaya)** — by opening an
issue, or by mentioning them on the issue or pull request where it happened.

**If the report should not be public, or if it concerns the owner**, use GitHub's own reporting route:
<https://github.com/contact/report-abuse>. That reaches GitHub Support rather than this project, and
GitHub can act on accounts and content independently of anyone here.

**There is deliberately no e-mail address in this file**, and you should know what that means before
you need it. An address in a public repository is harvested within days, and the studio's own business
address belongs to the business — it takes appointment enquiries and is not a place to send a report
about a comment on a pull request. The trade-off is that this project offers no private channel
directly to the maintainer; the GitHub route above is the private one, and it does not run through
this repository.

Reports are handled by the owner, who is the only person with any authority here. In practice that
means hiding or deleting comments, blocking accounts from the repository, and reporting to GitHub —
the actions GitHub itself provides, taken by the person able to take them.

*(Security vulnerabilities are a different thing and have their own route: see
[`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md). Do not report those as a public issue.)*

## Attribution

This code of conduct adopts the Contributor Covenant, version 2.1, available at
<https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html>. The Covenant's enforcement
guidelines are inspired by Mozilla's code of conduct enforcement ladder.
